raw:
Ashara swings her practice jacket over one shoulder. “Fine. Orientation starts at eight. The Academy doesn’t care whether you’ve had time to prepare.”

Rashid is already crossing into the common room. Dena deals him a hand without looking up.

“You’re late,” she says.

“I’m aware.”

“Good. It saves time.”

Ashara heads out through the front doors toward the quadrangle, her boots sharp against the stone. The moment she is gone, the dining hall feels less arranged around her.

The library is quieter than the rest of the house: lamp-oil, paper, old wood, and the faint metallic smell of rain carried in whenever someone uses the garden door. Blue-spined course volumes fill one low shelf beneath a sign marked **FIRST-YEAR CONCLAVE**.

You find procedure, comparative arcana, and a calendar dense with seminars, assessments, meals, and formal obligations. *Procedures and Precedents* is mostly about who speaks when, how objections are recorded, and the many ways a Council argument can become official without anyone raising their voice. The arcana survey devotes chapters to life-force discipline, ritual, consent, and the slower workings of elven spellcraft.

Its human chapter is four pages long.

Most of it concerns arbitration and translation. The final paragraph notes that human comparative-magic instruction is “pending restoration of qualified faculty and students.”

At a central table beneath the spiral stair, a man in a dark coat works through a stack of brittle papers with a magnifying lens. A small brass plaque identifies him as **Professor Gareth Stone — Human Covenant History**.

The card game rises and falls faintly through the wall: Dena accusing someone of inventing rules, then several people laughing at once.

Professor Stone closes his folder. He looks at the Garvey signet, then at the blue-spined book open before you.

“Mr. Garvey,” he says. “Did the Academy give you the reading list for my seminar?”
